info.title: Harbour API
info.description: Internal API for the Harbour web and mobile apps. Every request is scoped to one organisation (x-harbour-tenant) and enforced again by Postgres row-level security.

bearerAuth.description: Session token from the set-auth-token header (mobile app)

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem details with a stable code

device.description: User agent of the signed-in device

code.description: SNOMED CT concept id (Accessible Information Standard)

ResuscitationStatus.description: The CPR decision in force from a DNACPR or ReSPECT record; 'not_recorded' when there is none, never blank

RecordHistory.description: Human-readable history of a mutable record

StaffName.description: A member of staff named for attribution on a record the caller may read: display name and job title

PersonInvolvement.description: Regulation 9: how the person took part

CloseKeyIssue.description: The day the key came back, or was reported lost

CloseSharingDecision.description: Withdraw, suspend or lift a suspension, with the reason

SharingVisibility.description: What one recipient may see now: closed unless a decision in force covers it

TaskTimeState.description: Where the task stands now, from its window and status

Recurrence.description: UK local times; every_hours counts elapsed hours

DocumentItem.description: Document metadata; the bytes are at /content

RetentionCandidate.description: A document past retention with no legal hold

DestructionResult.description: Certificates per record class; skipped ids were held, not yet due or not found

EscalationPolicyRef.description: The organisation's own escalation policy for a validated tool's result, or that none is configured; never a Harbour recommendation

FluidDay.description: Fluid balance for one UK calendar day (00:00 to 24:00)

BodyMapViewerZone.description: The left of the drawing, its centre band, or its right, as the person recording saw it

CarePlanDue.description: What is due next: the first plan, then its review

outcome.description: The outcome in the person's words

PcspDomain.description: The 16 need domains of the care and support plan

UpdateRiskAssessment.description: A review: the whole assessment as it now stands

CreateAssessment.description: Answers to a locked validated tool; the server calculates and stores the result. A correction names the result it supersedes and why.

VisitKind.description: Regulation 9A: visiting, visits out and accompaniment

UpdateAdvanceCareRecord.description: A changed CPR decision is a new record, which supersedes this one

CreateEscalationPolicyLink.description: Links the organisation's escalation policy to a validated tool, for one band or every band, for one location or the whole organisation

CreateDiscardReason.description: Adds a coded reason for deleting unsent entries on a device

name.description: The shift's name in the location's pattern

area.description: Floor or unit; null for people with no room

action.description: What staff do, as the plan words it

PlanActionRef.description: The care plan action a round carries out

action.description: What staff do, as the active plan words it

NotARound.description: An action of the person's active plan that generates no rounds (medicines, until the eMAR), listed so the round never reads as the whole of their care

at.description: When it happened, or when the task fell due

HandoverItemKind.description: In order of how urgently the next shift needs it

CreateConsent.description: The person's capacity for the decision is found from their capacity assessments, never taken from the request.

IncidentSeverity.description: NPSA consequence scale, as staff judge it

HarmGrade.description: LFPSE physical harm, as staff judge it

validUntil.description: After this the pack says it is out of date

notice.description: The words at the top of every page, now

pages.description: One page per person receiving care, in room order (DowntimePersonPage)

DowntimePackOut.description: A location's downtime pack, with its freshness worked out now (HZ-021)

SyncToken.description: Short-lived PowerSync token scoped to tenant and assignments

SyncDiscard.description: A device deleted, or is about to delete, entries that never reached the server; recorded as an audit event

DeviceBindingItem.description: A member of staff's use of a Care mode device, and whether it is revoked

RefusedEntryItem.description: The server's copy of an entry a device could not save

post.summary: Change a person's status (people.md rules 1 and 2)
post.description: Checked with checkPersonStatusChange: the permission, reason and step-up of the PERSON_LIFECYCLE move, a time neither in the future (beyond the clock-drift tolerance) nor before the current status began, a discharge that says whether it is a transfer, archiving only once the exit workflow has closed, and no re-admission after a death. Admission has its own route. The effects run in the same transaction: rounds paused or resumed, future tasks cancelled, sharing closed, the bed released or the room held, the exit workflow started or cancelled, and one outbox event. A death recorded in error is corrected with a reason and step-up (HZ-001).

post.summary: A short-lived token for the PowerSync service, scoped to tenant and assignments
post.description: Claims: sub, tenant_id, location_ids, people_location_ids, care_location_ids, entries_location_ids and handover_location_ids with people_assigned, care_assigned, entries_assigned and handover_assigned (each stream family where its own read permissions reach: people.person.read with care.plan.read, care.plan.read (also the round's open tasks), care.note.read and care.handover.manage), entries_write_location_ids and entries_write_assigned (where the phone may record: care.note.write) with entries_write_person_ids (the people the member is assigned to, when entries_write_assigned, up to 100), and offline_days (the offline window from the rate table, never from the device). The device the request names (x-harbour-device) is bound to the member; a device a manager revoked is refused with 403 device_revoked, which the device reads apart from an expired session (401) and the session codes.

post.summary: Record that a device deleted entries that never reached the server
post.description: Writes an append-only audit event for one stage of a deletion (requested, deleted or failed): who deleted them, whose they were, the coded reason, how many and from which device (HZ-040). Anyone but the caller's own entries, deleted by the caller, needs a manager's permission. Each stage of an id is recorded once, and later stages must match the first (kind and owner) and come from its sender, the owner or a manager. Each person starts at most 20 deletion records a day. A deletion recorded as deleted closes the hold tasks of the device it names (or the sender's) when the sender owns the hold, raised its task or can act on it there, and listed entries already on the server are counted on one review task for the record.

post.summary: A device's unsent work: counts and the oldest age, no personal data
post.description: Writes an audit event with the device's queued, refused, held and blocked counts and the age of the oldest, so the server knows what a lost or wiped device held (HZ-006). Any member of the organisation may report (with MFA when their roles call for it), so a device whose Care mode access was withdrawn can still report its hold. A named owner counts only when bound to the device (a sync token issued to it or a report sent from it, kept as a device binding); otherwise the claim is recorded and changes nothing. Times later than the server's are taken as the server's, and a hold's start is never earlier than the device's last report for it said, nor than the server first saw the device. While anything waits, the device has a task for the Registered Manager at each location of its sync scope where the hold's owner or the reporter works, due when its hold escalates and never moved later; one closed in the last day is reopened, its escalation reset at most once a day. A report with nothing waiting closes them when it comes from the hold's owner, from whoever raised them or from a manager at one of their locations. Each reporter raises tasks for a few devices a day; past that, their holds join one task for that reporter, due at the earliest of them.

post.summary: Revoke a lost or withdrawn Care mode device
post.description: Marks every binding of the device revoked with a coded reason (step-up). At its next sync token or upload the device is refused with 403 device_revoked and wipes, keeping entries not yet sent under the hold rules. The sessions bound to it are not ended: every request from one is refused with 403 device_revoked whatever device it names, except its device report, which may raise or hurry the hold's task but never close it. When the device last reported entries waiting, the revocation needs confirmEntriesWaiting (409 entries_waiting otherwise), and its hold's task falls due at once, urgent, with a notice to the manager. A device already revoked changes nothing but hurries that task again. A device no member the caller manages has used reads as not found; a location role may not revoke a device staff it does not manage have also used.

post.summary: Keep the server's copy of a care entry the API refused from a device
post.description: Stores the request a device made for an entry the API refused (checked against that entry kind's own contract), once per entry id, with the refusal (in the owner's name when a manager hands over another member's held entries, as for the entry routes), and adds it to the person's one open review task for the nurse in charge (due at once; urgent, with a notice to the nurse in charge, when an observation joins it). A copy about a person is taken only when its author cared for them within the offline window; otherwise, as for a person unknown here, it is refused the same way. Written in the organisation's view, so a copy is kept even when its author can no longer see the person; read like the care record. A revoked device's copies come only with a hand-over, and a handed-over copy is checked against the device's hold like the entry it is (its owner's care judged from the entry's own time). Each author's copies count against 200 a day, after the replay check.
